title: Moderna Science Day: Company Unveils In Vivo CAR-T and T-Cell Engager Programs, Pitches 'Multi-Modality' Pivot
detail: At its June 25, 2026 Science Day, Moderna showcased an expanding mRNA pipeline reaching beyond vaccines into oncology, autoimmune disease, and rare conditions. The company introduced an in vivo CAR-T modality, mRNA-6007, entering early development for B-cell-mediated autoimmune diseases with an initial clinical focus on systemic lupus erythematosus; the multiplexed mRNA/lipid-nanoparticle approach aims to deliver transient CAR expression directly in vivo, avoiding the manufacturing complexity of ex vivo cell therapy. Moderna also highlighted validation of its T-cell engager modality via mRNA-2808 in multiple myeloma, supporting advancement of a second candidate, mRNA-2151, toward early development in ovarian cancer. CEO Stéphane Bancel framed the event as evidence Moderna is evolving into a 'diversified, multi-modality biotechnology company' built on its four approved products (Spikevax, mRESVIA, mNEXSPIKE, mCOMBRIAX) plus this expanding oncology/autoimmune/rare-disease pipeline. The announcement contributed to a sharp Moderna stock rally through late June, compounding gains from the June 18 FDA advisory committee win on its flu vaccine.
